name: External financial statement audit of a mid-size private company
summary: An accounting firm audits the annual financial statements of a mid-size private company, usually because its lenders or investors require an audit opinion within about 120 days of year end. The firm first decides whether to keep the client and confirms independence, then plans the audit, tests controls and transactions at an interim visit, and after year end tests balances using documents the client provides and confirmations from banks and customers. Work passes up through senior, manager and partner review, and for higher-risk clients through a second partner's quality review, before the partner signs the opinion and the file is archived within 60 days. Most of the elapsed time is calendar waiting for year end and for the client's close, and late or incomplete client schedules and rounds of review notes are the usual causes of delay.

baseline.org_archetype: A regional US CPA firm with an audit practice of about 50 to 60 people auditing private companies with $25 million to $500 million of revenue, using electronic workpaper software and a client request portal or spreadsheet.
baseline.notes: The unit is one annual audit under AICPA generally accepted auditing standards (AU-C), not a PCAOB audit. The client's own staff time is outside the firm and is shown only as waiting.

unit_of_work: one annual financial statement audit engagement for one private company
trigger: The firm's annual continuance cycle (or a new client's request for proposal) starts the acceptance or continuance evaluation, usually three to five months before the client's year end.
end_state: The partner has signed and released the audit opinion with governance letters, and the final audit file is assembled and locked; or the engagement is declined.

volume.seasonality: Strongly seasonal: most private clients have December year ends, so planning peaks in September to November, fieldwork in February to April, and report release in March to April near the 120-day lender deadline.

evidence.note: Estimate for a regional firm office auditing about 100 private companies a year (an average of 8 engagements starting a month). FERF 2015 shows most private respondents use large regional firms rather than the Big 4.

triggered_by.from: Prospective client or lender requiring an audit
triggered_by.object: request for proposal or audit requirement

produces.object: audited financial statements with auditor's report

produces.to: Lenders and investors of the client
produces.object: audited financial statements for covenant compliance
governance communication and internal control deficiency letter
archived audit file and final billing

produces.to: Prospective client or lender requiring an audit

evidence.note: Partners are owners whose pay is above the BLS 90th percentile ($62.01); a cost of $150 to $280 an hour assumes partner income of roughly $250,000 to $450,000 with overhead. Estimate.
A partner not on the engagement; cost assumed equal to an engagement partner.

systems.name: Client request list (spreadsheet or client portal)
Firm independence and client acceptance system
Client accounting system and trial balance export
Spreadsheets for analytics and lead schedules
Practice management, scheduling and time and billing
Financial statement drafting and disclosure checklist tool

steps.name: Prepare acceptance or continuance evaluation
steps.description: The audit manager completes the firm's acceptance or continuance form: management integrity, changes in ownership or financing, going concern indicators, the firm's competence and staffing in the industry, prior-year issues, fee collection and whether the engagement meets the firm's criteria for an engagement quality control review.

error.defect_description: A risk factor such as new debt covenants or a related-party change is not identified.

control.basis: AICPA quality control standards (QC 10) and AU-C 220A.14: acceptance and continuance procedures followed and concluded on

evidence.note: AU-C 220A requires acceptance and continuance procedures; JofA describes EQR criteria considered at acceptance. Times are estimates.

steps.name: Confirm independence of firm and team
steps.description: The audit senior checks the firm's independence system for financial interests, other services the firm provides to the client and fee dependence, collects independence confirmations from each planned team member, and documents any safeguards for non-attest services such as drafting the financial statements.

error.defect_description: A non-attest service is not evaluated for independence threats.

control.basis: AICPA Code of Professional Conduct independence rule (ET 1.200) and nonattest services requirements (ET 1.295)

evidence.note: Independence confirmation is a standard part of acceptance; the step layout and times are estimates.

steps.name: Partner approves acceptance or continuance
steps.description: The engagement partner reads the continuance form and independence documentation, considers fee and risk, and approves continuing, refers a high-risk client to the firm's risk management partner, or declines the engagement.

error.defect_description: None introduced; errors pass through.

control.basis: AU-C 220A.14 and firm quality control policy: engagement partner concludes on acceptance and continuance

next.condition: high-risk client referred to risk management
firm declines or client changes auditor

evidence.note: Shares are estimates.

steps.name: Risk management partner approves high-risk client
steps.description: A partner from the firm's quality and risk function reviews the high-risk acceptance form, may require an engagement quality control review or added specialists, and approves or rejects the engagement.

error.defect_description: None introduced; errors pass through.

control.basis: Firm quality control policy: second partner approval for clients above the firm's acceptance risk threshold

evidence.note: JofA lists high-risk engagements under firm acceptance criteria as a common trigger for added quality review. Times are estimates.

steps.name: Draft and send engagement letter
steps.description: The audit manager drafts the engagement letter from the firm template with the objective, management's responsibilities, the reporting framework, fees, timing and any non-attest services, and emails it to the client's chief financial officer for signature.

error.defect_description: Responsibilities for non-attest services or the reporting deadline stated incorrectly.

control.basis: AU-C 210: terms of the audit engagement agreed with management and documented in an engagement letter

evidence.note: AU-C 210 requires agreeing terms with management in an engagement letter. Times are estimates.

steps.name: Client signs engagement letter
steps.description: The client's chief financial officer and sometimes the owner or board chair review the fee and terms, may negotiate the fee, and sign and return the engagement letter.

error.defect_description: None introduced; errors pass through.

next.condition: client does not sign and seeks another auditor

evidence.note: Estimate based on common practice.

steps.name: Update understanding of the entity and its controls
steps.description: The audit senior reads board minutes, contracts and interim financial statements, interviews the controller about changes in the business, systems and staff, performs walkthroughs of revenue, purchasing, payroll and the close process, and runs preliminary analytics on the interim trial balance.

error.defect_description: A change in a process or a new revenue stream is not captured, so a risk is under-assessed.

control.basis: AU-C 315: understanding the entity, its environment and internal control to identify and assess risks of material misstatement

evidence.note: Required by AU-C 315. Hours scaled to a median private-company audit of about 850 hours (FERF 2015); the split is an estimate. Planning is scheduled two to four months before year end.

steps.name: Assess risks, set materiality and design the audit plan
steps.description: The audit manager sets overall and performance materiality, identifies significant risks such as revenue recognition and management override, decides the controls and substantive approach for each area, and tailors the audit programs, sample sizes and the client request list.

error.defect_description: Materiality set too high or a significant risk missed, leading to too little testing.

control.basis: AU-C 300 planning, AU-C 320 materiality and AU-C 330 responses to assessed risks

evidence.note: Required by AU-C 300, 320 and 330. Times are estimates.

steps.name: Partner approves the audit plan
steps.description: The engagement partner reviews the risk assessment, materiality and planned procedures, holds the planning discussion with the team about fraud risks, confirms whether an engagement quality control review is needed, and signs off the plan.

error.defect_description: None introduced; errors pass through.

control.basis: AU-C 220A.17 and AU-C 300: engagement partner responsible for direction and supervision and for the planning discussion including fraud (AU-C 240)

next.condition: partner asks for changes to risk assessment or scope

evidence.note: AU-C 220A makes the partner responsible for direction and supervision; JofA notes the EQR decision is usually made by planning. Shares are estimates.

steps.name: Issue client request list and fieldwork schedule
steps.description: The audit senior sends the client the prepared-by-client request list with due dates for reconciliations, schedules, contracts and support, and agrees the interim and year-end fieldwork dates and the inventory count date with the controller.

error.defect_description: Request list carried forward from last year without updates, so new items are requested late.

evidence.note: Connor Group describes the PBC list arriving from auditors before books close. Times are estimates.

steps.name: Perform interim fieldwork
steps.description: Staff auditors test the design and implementation of key controls, select and test interim samples of revenue, purchases and payroll, read contracts and update permanent files, working at the client site or remotely with documents the client uploads.

error.defect_description: Samples or tests documented incompletely, for example a sign-off without evidence of what was examined.

evidence.note: Hours scaled to the FERF 2015 private-company median of 850 audit hours; JofA 2017 reports documentation deficiencies such as sign-offs without evidence. Timing and split are estimates.

steps.name: Send external confirmations and legal letters at year end
steps.description: Shortly after year end the audit senior selects customer balances, banks and lenders and the client's outside lawyers, prepares confirmation and legal inquiry letters, gets client authorization, and sends them through the confirmation platform or by mail while keeping control of the requests.

error.defect_description: Wrong address or contact used, causing non-response or a confirmation sent to the client instead of the third party.

control.basis: AU-C 505 external confirmations (auditor maintains control over requests) and AU-C 501 inquiry of the entity's legal counsel

evidence.note: AU-C 505 requires the auditor to control confirmation requests. The wait is the calendar gap from interim fieldwork to year end; estimate.

steps.name: Observe the physical inventory count
steps.description: One or two staff auditors attend the client's year-end inventory count at the warehouse, observe count procedures, perform test counts from the floor to the count sheets and back, and record cutoff information on the last receipts and shipments.

error.defect_description: Test counts not traced to the final inventory listing.

control.basis: AU-C 501: attendance at physical inventory counting when inventory is material

evidence.note: AU-C 501 requires attendance at counting when inventory is material. The 45% share is an estimate for mid-size private companies.

steps.name: Client closes the books and provides year-end schedules
steps.description: The client's accounting team closes the year, posts accruals and reconciliations, and uploads the trial balance and the requested schedules and support; items arrive over several weeks and some are missing or do not agree to the ledger.

error.defect_description: Schedules that do not agree to the trial balance or lack support.

evidence.note: Connor Group: schedules arriving without workpapers and reconciliations kicked back push the audit. The close duration and 70% share are estimates.

steps.name: Chase outstanding client items
steps.description: The audit senior updates the request tracker, emails and calls the controller about missing or inconsistent items, explains what support is needed, and reschedules fieldwork areas that cannot start.

error.defect_description: None introduced; errors pass through.

evidence.note: Practitioner description of late client schedules. Shares and waits are estimates.

steps.name: Perform year-end substantive testing
steps.description: Staff auditors test year-end balances: agree confirmations and perform alternative procedures for non-responses, test revenue cutoff and samples, accruals, payables search, fixed assets, debt and equity, payroll and inventory pricing, and document each test in the workpaper software.

error.defect_description: Incomplete testing or documentation, or exceptions not followed up.

control.basis: AU-C 330 and AU-C 500: sufficient appropriate audit evidence for each material balance; AU-C 230 documentation

evidence.note: Largest share of the median 850 private-company audit hours; the split is an estimate. Elapsed time is roughly two to three weeks with two or three staff.

steps.name: Test complex areas and review staff work
steps.description: The audit senior performs the judgmental areas such as revenue contracts, reserves, estimates and going concern analysis, and gives first-level review to each staff workpaper, sending notes back for missing evidence or explanations.

error.defect_description: An estimate is accepted without enough challenge of management's assumptions.

control.basis: Firm review policy under AU-C 220A.18: work of less experienced staff reviewed by more experienced team members

evidence.note: AU-C 220A makes the partner responsible for reviews per firm policy; tiered senior, manager, partner review is common practice. Hours are estimates.

steps.name: Manager review of workpapers
steps.description: The audit manager reviews the workpapers area by area, checks that significant risks were addressed, compares results to expectations, and writes review notes asking for more testing, support or explanation.

error.defect_description: Review note not raised on an under-supported area.

control.basis: Firm review policy under AU-C 220A.18

evidence.note: Managers carry several engagements in busy season, so files wait days for review; estimate.

steps.name: Clear review notes with client support
steps.description: The audit senior and staff respond to each review note, ask the client for added support or explanations, perform extra procedures where needed, and update the workpapers for re-review.

error.defect_description: A note is closed with an explanation but no evidence.

next.condition: manager re-reviews and raises further notes

evidence.note: Waits for client answers; shares are estimates.

steps.name: Propose adjustments and agree them with management
steps.description: The audit manager summarizes proposed audit adjustments and uncorrected misstatements, discusses them with the controller and chief financial officer, and gets management to record the adjustments or confirm in writing why uncorrected items are immaterial.

error.defect_description: An adjustment is recorded by the client differently from what was proposed.

control.basis: AU-C 450: evaluation and communication of misstatements identified during the audit

evidence.note: Required by GAAS; times are estimates.

steps.name: Prepare draft financial statements and disclosure checklist
steps.description: The audit senior prepares or reviews the draft financial statements and notes from the adjusted trial balance, ties every number to the workpapers, and completes the disclosure checklist for the reporting framework.

error.defect_description: Tie-out error or missing disclosure, for example on leases or revenue disaggregation.

evidence.note: Many mid-size private clients rely on the auditor to draft the statements as a non-attest service; estimate.

steps.name: Client reviews and approves the draft financial statements
steps.description: The client's chief financial officer and owners read the draft statements and notes, ask questions, request wording changes, and approve the statements and the recorded adjustments as management's responsibility.

error.defect_description: None introduced; errors pass through.

evidence.note: Estimate based on common practice.

steps.name: Partner review of the file and financial statements
steps.description: The engagement partner reviews the significant risk areas, the summary memo, uncorrected misstatements, going concern conclusion and the draft statements and report, discusses issues with the manager, and writes partner review notes.

error.defect_description: A judgment issue passes review.

control.basis: AU-C 220A.19: on or before the report date the engagement partner is satisfied through review that sufficient appropriate evidence supports the report

next.condition: signed off; no quality control review required
signed off; engagement quality control review required

evidence.note: AU-C 220A.19 requires partner review before the report date. JofA 2001: lag rises when hours exceed budget. Shares are estimates.

steps.name: Engagement quality control review
steps.description: A partner who is not on the engagement discusses significant findings with the engagement partner, reads the financial statements and proposed report, reviews selected workpapers on the significant judgments, and either clears the review or raises issues that must be resolved before release.

error.defect_description: None introduced; errors pass through.

control.basis: AU-C 220A.21 to .22 and firm quality control criteria (QC 10): report not released until the engagement quality control review is complete

next.condition: issues raised that require more work

evidence.note: AU-C 220A.21 to .22 define the review and require completion before release; firms set the criteria, so the 20% share is an estimate.

steps.name: Complete subsequent events and completion procedures
steps.description: The audit senior updates subsequent events inquiries and reads minutes through the expected report date, follows up legal letter responses, completes the completion checklist and drafts the management representation letter and governance communications.

error.defect_description: A subsequent event such as a covenant waiver or lawsuit is not captured.

control.basis: AU-C 560 subsequent events and AU-C 501 legal letters through the report date

evidence.note: Required by GAAS; times are estimates.

steps.name: Management signs the representation letter
steps.description: The client's chief executive and chief financial officer read and sign the representation letter dated as of the report date, confirming the completeness of information and their responsibility for the financial statements.

error.defect_description: None introduced; errors pass through.

control.basis: AU-C 580: written representations dated as of the date of the auditor's report

evidence.note: AU-C 580 requires representations dated as of the report date. Wait is an estimate.

steps.name: Partner signs and releases the report
steps.description: The engagement partner confirms all review notes and the quality review are cleared, signs and dates the auditor's report, releases the audited statements to the client, and issues the governance letter and any internal control deficiency letter.

error.defect_description: None introduced; errors pass through.

control.basis: AU-C 700 report signed by the firm through a licensed CPA partner; AU-C 260 and 265 communications to those charged with governance

evidence.note: Report release usually lands 90 to 120 days after year end to meet lender deadlines.

steps.name: Assemble and lock the final audit file
steps.description: The audit senior removes superseded drafts, checks that every workpaper is signed off by preparer and reviewer, archives the electronic file so later changes are logged, and records the documentation completion date.

error.defect_description: Missing sign-offs found later in inspection or peer review.

control.basis: AU-C 230: final audit file assembled no later than 60 days after the report release date and retained at least five years

evidence.note: AU-C 230 sets the 60-day assembly limit; teams typically archive after busy season, so the wait is an estimate.

exceptions.name: High-risk client acceptance
exceptions.description: Risk factors such as going concern doubt, a new owner or a regulated industry send the acceptance to the firm's risk management partner, who may impose a quality review.

exceptions.name: Engagement declined
exceptions.description: The firm or its risk partner declines, or the client does not sign the engagement letter and moves to another auditor.

exceptions.name: Inventory count observation
exceptions.description: The client holds material inventory, so staff must attend the year-end count at the warehouse.

exceptions.name: Late or incomplete client schedules
exceptions.description: Client items arrive late, do not agree to the ledger or lack support, and the senior has to chase them, sometimes more than once, before fieldwork can proceed.

exceptions.name: Second round of manager review notes
exceptions.description: After notes are cleared the manager re-reviews and raises further notes, adding several days.

exceptions.name: Partner or quality reviewer sends file back
exceptions.description: Partner review or the engagement quality control review raises issues, for example on an estimate or going concern, that need more work and evidence.

exceptions.name: Engagement quality control review
exceptions.description: The engagement meets the firm's criteria (high risk, new client, specialized industry, going concern) and a second partner must clear it before release.

exceptions.name: Going concern or modified opinion
exceptions.description: Covenant breaches or losses raise substantial doubt; the team obtains management's plans and lender waivers, consults within the firm, and may add an emphasis paragraph or modify the opinion, extending partner and quality review.

benchmarks.unit: calendar days from start of acceptance or continuance to locked audit file
benchmarks.population: Annual audits of mid-size US private companies with December year ends (author's synthesis)

evidence.note: Synthesis: continuance and planning start three to five months before year end (estimate); audited statements are typically due to lenders 90 to 120 days after year end (Connor Group, Clifford Chance); AU-C 230 allows up to 60 days after release to assemble the file. 120 + 105 + 35 days gives about 260 to 280 days.

benchmarks.unit: days from fiscal year end to delivery of audited statements required by loan agreements
benchmarks.population: Private companies with bank or leveraged loans

evidence.note: Contractual deadlines, not measured report dates.

benchmarks.unit: audit firm hours per annual audit
benchmarks.population: 30 US private companies reporting hours, FERF 2015 (fiscal 2014)

evidence.note: Small self-selected sample; the mean is pulled up by large companies.

benchmarks.unit: audit firm hours per annual audit
benchmarks.population: 118 US private companies, FEI survey FY2012

benchmarks.unit: share of engagements reviewed in AICPA enhanced oversight
benchmarks.population: Peer-reviewed engagements selected for enhanced oversight

pain_points.description: Client schedules arrive late, incomplete or not agreeing to the ledger, so fieldwork starts late or stops while the senior chases items.

Review happens in layers (senior, manager, partner, sometimes a quality reviewer) on managers and partners who carry many engagements in busy season, so files wait days for each review and notes come back in rounds.

evidence.note: JofA 2001 finds lag rises when hours run over budget.

pain_points.description: Documentation is often incomplete, for example program sign-offs without evidence of the test, which peer review flags as material nonconformity.

evidence.note: One in four engagements in enhanced oversight were materially nonconforming for documentation.

pain_points.description: Busy-season compression: most clients share a December year end and a 120-day lender deadline, so fieldwork for many clients overlaps in February to April.
Confirmation non-responses force alternative procedures and follow-up.

evidence.note: Common practice; no rate was sourced.

sources.title: AICPA Professional Standards: AU-C Sections (Statements on Auditing Standards, currently effective)
sources.supports: AU-C 210: auditor agrees terms of the engagement with management in an engagement letter. AU-C 220A (effective for the reference period): engagement partner satisfied that acceptance and continuance procedures were followed; partner takes responsibility for reviews and, on or before the report date, reviews documentation; an engagement quality control review is required only for engagements meeting the firm's criteria and must be completed before the report is released. AU-C 230: final file assembled no later than 60 days after the report release date; retention at least five years. AU-C 505: auditor maintains control over confirmation requests. AU-C 580: written representations dated as of the auditor's report date.

sources.title: Engagement quality reviews: What auditors should know
sources.supports: Firms set their own criteria for engagement quality reviews, for example high-risk engagements, unmodified reports with going concern issues, new clients, specialized industries; the need is usually decided by planning; the review is completed on or before the report date and should not be rushed at the end.

sources.title: Audit documentation: Tips for getting it right
sources.supports: AICPA enhanced oversight found one in four engagements materially nonconforming because of inadequate audit documentation; sign-off on an audit program is rarely sufficient documentation.

sources.title: 2015 Audit Fee Report
sources.supports: 92 private companies (most with revenue of $100 million to $499 million) paid an average audit fee of $254,740 and median of $70,000 for 2014; 30 reported audit hours, average 2,800 and median 850, about $159 per hour on average; 22.8% used the Big 4, most used large regional firms.

sources.title: US public, private companies report rise in audit fees in FY 2012
sources.supports: FEI survey of 118 private companies: FY2012 average audit fee $147,800 and average audit hours 1,769.

sources.title: Debt covenant deadlines are coming: How private companies prepare for the audit
sources.supports: (Publication date not shown; year approximate.) Audited financial statements are typically due to lenders 90 to 120 days after year end, sometimes 150 or 180 days; the PBC list arrives before books close; late schedules, kicked-back reconciliations and new audit requests push the timeline.

sources.title: Coronavirus: leveraged finance, key considerations in respect of delayed audits and reporting covenants
sources.supports: Loan arrangements generally require annual audited financial reports within 120 days of fiscal year end, in some cases 90 or 150 days.

sources.title: Research summary: audit report lag
sources.supports: Study of 226 engagements at an international firm: audit report lag increased when actual hours exceeded budget and when tax services were included; a higher share of manager and partner hours reduced lag.

sources.title: Occupational Employment and Wages, May 2021: 13-2011 Accountants and Auditors
sources.supports: Mean hourly wage $40.37; 10th percentile $23.06, 25th $29.21, median $37.14, 75th $47.98, 90th $62.01; mean $41.66 in accounting, tax preparation, bookkeeping and payroll services.

sources.title: Employer Costs for Employee Compensation, December 2020
sources.supports: Private industry management, professional and related occupations: total compensation $61.72 per hour, wages $42.95, benefits 30.4% of compensation.

assumptions: The engagement is a recurring audit (85%) of a private company with $25 million to $500 million revenue and a December year end, performed by a regional CPA firm under AICPA AU-C standards.

Firm hours per engagement average about 800 to 900, matching the FERF 2015 private-company median of 850 hours; the split across partner (about 5%), manager (about 10%), senior (about 30%) and staff (about 55%) is the author's estimate.

The simulator adds hands-on minutes to elapsed time as if one person worked around the clock; real fieldwork is done by two or three staff over working hours, which roughly offsets, so no extra wait was added for fieldwork duration.
Client staff time (preparing schedules, answering questions) is real but outside the firm; it is shown as external waits with zero firm hands-on time.
The share of engagements needing an engagement quality control review (about 20 to 25%) is an estimate; AU-C 220A leaves the criteria to each firm and some small firms review none.

The cycle-time benchmark is a synthesis from lender deadlines (90 to 120 days after year end), an assumed start three to five months before year end, and the AU-C 230 60-day assembly window; no measured distribution of private-company report dates was found.
Volume of 8 engagements a month is an annual average for a regional office; in practice starts cluster in late summer and autumn.
Loaded costs use BLS May 2021 wages for accountants and auditors times about 1.7; partner cost is an estimate because partner income is not published by BLS.
The web search budget ran out during research, so confirmation response times and review-note statistics could not be sourced and are estimates.
